prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- If you want one tool to actively control how AI and search chatbots present your business, Yext (Knowledge Graph + AI integrations) is the best single commercial choice.
- If you want an affordable monitoring + local SEO solution to check visibility and recommendations across search and review platforms, BrightLocal (or Moz Local / Whitespark) is the best practical choice.
- For checking ChatGPT/Bard/Bing Chat specifically, there’s no single automated "AI recommendation scanner" — you should both test the models directly and make sure your business data is accurate, structured, and widely listed.

Why those recommendations
- Yext: built to publish and maintain authoritative business data across dozens of platforms and has explicit integrations and positioning for AI/chat features so you can influence what models surface.
- BrightLocal / Moz Local / Whitespark: lower-cost tools that track local SEO, listings, and rankings across directories and search engines — useful to see whether your business is being surfaced for local queries that AI may draw on.
- No universal scanner for LLM recommendations: LLMs like ChatGPT do not rely on a single public index you can query; their outputs depend on training data, browsing plugins (if enabled), and third‑party connectors. That means testing models directly is necessary.

Practical steps you can take now
1. Claim and optimize the big listings (free, high ROI)
   - Google Business Profile, Apple Maps (Maps Connect), Bing Places, Yelp, Facebook/Meta.
2. Add structured data to your website
   - Add Schema.org LocalBusiness, FAQPage and QAPage markup so search engines and crawlers (and some AI tools) can extract authoritative facts.
3. Use a listings management tool
   - Yext (control/authority + AI-focused integrations)
   - BrightLocal / Moz Local / Whitespark (monitoring, citation building, rank tracking)
4. Monitor mentions and reviews
   - Google Alerts, Mention, Brand24, or the monitoring features in BrightLocal/SEMrush.
5. Test chat AIs directly and regularly
   - Ask: “Recommend three [service] providers in [city], and why.” Try the same prompt in ChatGPT, Bing Chat, and Google Bard. Save results to track changes over time.
   - Use the OpenAI or other APIs to automate periodic queries if you want scheduled checks.
6. Provide high-quality, authoritative content
   - A clear services page, FAQ, pricing, contact/booking options, and structured data increase the chance AIs will recommend your business.
7. Consider a “knowledge graph” or chatbot on your site
   - Yext Answers, a site search/FAQ bot, or a custom GPT (if you use OpenAI tools) can surface your business as an authoritative answer directly to users.

Which to pick for different goals
- If your goal is to control how AI/chatbots present facts about your business: Yext (enterprise) is most directly built for that.
- If your goal is to monitor local visibility and get actionable SEO improvements on a modest budget: BrightLocal or Moz Local.
- If your goal is simply to see whether ChatGPT/Bard recommend you right now: manually query the models (or script queries via APIs) and iterate on listings/structured data.

If you want, tell me:
- which markets/platforms you care about (Google only vs. global directories),
- your budget (free vs. paid),
and I’ll recommend a specific plan and sample prompts/scripts you can run to test ChatGPT and other models.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
